title: OA ChatCompletions compatibility converter & fidelity gateway
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a compatibility/conversion layer that accepts OpenAI Chat Completions (OA-CC) style requests and responses and reliably maps them to Redwoods internal inference API and streaming protocol. This ticket covers the converter gateway, fidelity checks, and edge-case handling for message shapes, function/tool calling, structured outputs, stop-sequence behavior, and incremental (streamed) events. Goal: allow existing OA-CC client SDKs and integrations to operate against Redwood with minimal client changes while preserving telemetry and operational guarantees.
proposed_solution: Create a stateless gateway service (oa-cc-converter) that performs: 1) request normalization (roles, names, system prompts, function signatures), 2) mapping to Redwood internal call format including hints for kernel selection and caching keys, 3) streaming response re-framing (delta tokens, tool_call events, function outputs) back into OA-CC compatible SSE/HTTP chunks. Add a fidelity guard that validates incompatible patterns and returns informative 4xx errors or degraded responses based on configured compatibility policy. Provide feature flags to enable strict vs permissive compatibility modes.
streaming_semantics: Map OA-CC streaming frames (data: {"choices": [{"delta": {...}}]}) to Redwood streaming events: token.delta, token.complete, tool.call.start, tool.call.chunk, tool.call.end, structured.output.schema. Implementation must preserve event ordering and provide idempotency keys for client reconnection. For clients using chunked HTTP (non-SSE), support HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming with the OA-CC framing. For SSE streams, emit identical event lines and use the same top-level keys to avoid client-side parsers breaking. Ensure that partial function call arguments are emitted as successive tool.call.chunk events and the final call is a tool.call.end with assembled arguments. Backpressure: honor Redwood runtime backpressure signals and translate to OA-CC 'retry-after' headers or stream-level control messages when needed.
function_call_mapping: OA-CC function_call payloads (name + arguments string) will be parsed and canonicalized into Redwood tool invocation objects with: tool_name (string), tool_id (if available via model catalog), args_json (validated against function schema if provided), call_mode (sync/async). On responses where the model requests function_call, the gateway should: 1) emit an OA-style function_call event to the client stream, 2) optionally attempt internal tool invocation if configured for server-side tool execution, and 3) translate tool responses back to OA-formatted text or structured function_return events. Edge cases: malformed JSON in arguments -> return function_call.error with parse_error code; name mismatches -> return unmapped_tool warning and suggest candidate tools via telemetry.
structured_output_mapping: When OA clients use "structured" outputs (JSON schema, format instructions), gateway will attach a schema_id and validation_mode to the Redwood request. Redwood responses that produce structured tokens will be collected server-side and validated against the original schema. If validation fails, the gateway emits an OA-style message with diagnostics and a best-effort repaired JSON in an additional assistant message. Add a 'structured_validation' header to responses that indicates 'valid'|'partial'|'invalid' and include a human-readable 'repair_suggestion' string when applicable. For models returning tool-like structured blobs, map them into OA content under choices[].message with role 'assistant' and content as the serialized JSON, plus metadata in the 'finish_reason'.
telemetry_and_metrics: Add mapping-specific telemetry tags: compat.gateway.version, compat.mode (strict|permissive), mapping.latency_ms, streaming.reframes, function_call.parse_errors, structured.validation.status. Emit a trace span per incoming OA request showing time spent in: normalization, kernel-routing-hint injection, runtime-wait, streaming-reframe, and response-emit. Ensure per-customer tags are attached to enable cost/backpressure attribution. Track partial-replay-rate for reconnections and instrument counters for blocked incompatible patterns.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy gateway behind feature-flag to internal Redwood test accounts. 2) Enable permissive mode for 5 internal customers, monitor errors for 72 hours. 3) Switch to strict mode for a pilot customer with known OA compliance tests. 4) Gradual ramp to general availability across hosted API with opt-in through API header 'X-Compat-Mode'. 5) Add a deprecation timeline for OA behaviors we cannot map safely (list communicated via support). Rollback: feature-flag off; gateway should return 501 with guidance.
testing_plan: Unit tests: role/field mapping, malformed messages, streaming event order, function_call parsing, schema validation. Integration tests: end-to-end with Redwood runtime using a small curated model that emits function_call and structured JSON across streams; simulate reconnections and partial token delivery. Fuzz tests: random OA-style messages to confirm gateway never panics and returns well-formed error payloads. Performance tests: measure additional p50/p99 latency at 1k QPS and validate overhead <8ms p50 in permissive mode. Add compatibility test matrix in CI with OA SDK examples (python/openai-js).
open_questions: Should the gateway perform any automatic argument repair for badly-formed JSON or only surface errors?
Do we map OA function_call.name to Redwood tool_id automatically using model catalog aliases or require explicit mapping configuration per customer?
How should RBAC and customer keys map when a single request uses OA function_call that would trigger a downstream connector with different credentials?
